threads: Wow, new Django update. This is a major improvement for my business.
did you try it against a copy of production first?
yes, staging finally paid for itself. the migration was boring. beautiful.
PHP2Shell vulnerability just leaked; exploit in the works.
rumor or a working fingerprint match?
rumor for now. don't buy a packet off a screenshot.
GitHub is loaded with new Python libraries today, loving this.
my bookmarks grow faster than my free time
same. i maintain a requirements file for projects i haven't started.
Deploying a new LEMP stack. Apache is dead to me, but I see the appeal of LiteSpeed.
your next post will be about moving everything back
only if the config files apologize first.
Dropping a new exploit soon; SSH v2 is doomed!
which auth version and patch revision?
still testing. actual packets go through the traders, not my hype department.
just got sound working on the old laptop
what was wrong with it?
muted mixer. three hours. nobody speak to me.
gentoo compile started before dinner
what did you have?
breakfast, apparently.
anyone else still living inside screen?
screen inside ssh inside screen
that's not a workflow, that's a nesting doll.
finally convinced the office to try Linux
how did the printer take it?
personally.
my uptime was 200 days until someone found the power strip
a moment of silence for the counter
it was me. i wanted to plug in a kettle.
vim question: how do i leave
:q unless you've changed things
too late, i've become a maintainer.
i installed emacs for an editor
and how is the operating system?
great. still looking for the editor.
my backup script has been running flawlessly for months
you tested a restore, right?
brb, suddenly busy.
bought a secondhand ThinkPad. the keyboard has seen things.
does the red nub still work?
yes. it has more uptime than my server.
trying a tiling window manager tonight
how many terminals so far?
nine. still only doing one thing.
why is my web app slow
did you count the database queries?
i stopped at 400 and made tea.
found a bug in my shell script
quoting?
quoting. it's always quoting.
DNS finally propagated
was it actually DNS?
this time yes. i am as surprised as you are.
the server is down and the monitoring server says everything is fine
where is the monitoring server?
on the server. i see the problem.
put my dotfiles in git
including the weird aliases?
especially the weird aliases. future archaeologists deserve context.
new mechanical keyboard arrived
what switches?
the kind that get you banned from voice chat.
i miss forums with signatures bigger than the posts
and a little penguin saying what kernel you ran
mine also announced my RAM. all 256 megabytes of it.
irc over dialup had a certain atmosphere
that atmosphere was your modem negotiating
and everyone typing 'wb' when your connection came back.
built an entire weekend project in Python
what does it do?
organizes the directories containing my unfinished weekend projects.
the staging database is suspiciously empty
did you point the app at the right environment?
yes. the right environment was not impressed with my import script.
someone named the production host testbox
bold disaster recovery strategy
the actual test box is called do-not-touch.
finished reading the manual
all of it?
no. the part explaining where the rest of the manual is.
my laptop fan sounds like a small aircraft
compiling a kernel?
opening the company dashboard.
any good music for late-night maintenance?
ambient, no lyrics, no sudden alarms
so not the RAID controller's latest album.
got my first clean contract delivery
nice. remember to clear your local copies when the disk fills
already made a field note. not learning that one the hard way.
bought a lifetime exploit license
for which fingerprint?
exactly. i now understand why the trader asked that question twice.
the target got patched while i was offline
new scan, new intelligence
old license still works on the other hosts. lesson learned.
anyone keeping old underground zines?
box full of them. half the addresses are dead.
half is an excellent success rate around here.
switched my home server to BSD
how's it going?
quiet. suspiciously quiet. i keep checking if it's on.
my package manager wants to remove 80 packages
read the transaction summary before you say yes
for once i am reading every word.
tried a new color scheme
green on black?
green on slightly different black. radical stuff.
running a LAN party this weekend
will the network be ready?
the games are ready. the network is an ongoing philosophical discussion.
just replaced a dying disk
did SMART warn you?
SMART had been writing a novel. i finally read it.
my regex matches every test case
including the ones it shouldn't?
you had to ruin the moment.
someone committed a 400 MB log file
git remembers
so does everyone on this connection.
changed one config option, restarted three services
did it help?
not yet, but i have acquired four new log files.
the new intern asked why we still use IRC
what did you say?
because the channel has outlived six collaboration platforms.
i keep an emergency terminal open during upgrades
same. and a rescue USB nearby
and a second computer for pretending this was all planned.
found my old Linux install CDs
which distro?
three different ones, all labeled FINAL_THIS_ONE.
deploy finished with zero downtime
congrats!
i'm afraid to blink until the graphs settle.
the new library deleted half my application code
a successful refactor?
yes, this time intentionally.
just paid a trader through the channel
instant delivery?
yep. the bank ledger agrees. wish my real invoices worked like that.
PSA: shell access does not mean your logs are clean
someone had an exciting disconnect?
i would prefer the phrase educational disconnect.

reaction: The release notes are actually useful.
My business app might finally get a quiet weekend.
The smaller memory footprint caught my eye.
Finally, the behavior the docs promised.
The changelog deserves its own coffee break.
Looks promising; staging gets the first turn.
The maintainers earned a donation today.
Someone fixed my oldest bookmarked issue.
The defaults finally make sense to me.
Might be time to retire my local patch.
Going to wait for the first bugfix release, but I'm tempted.
outcome: the logs stayed boring, which is my favorite result
the test suite finally finished before my coffee went cold
the old workaround is gone and nothing caught fire
the deploy was uneventful for a change
i found a config typo i'd blamed on the software
the benchmark improved, but i'm keeping the old numbers too
the rollback worked when i tested it
i learned more from the migration notes than the announcement
the service survived a reboot; small victories
startup is faster and the monitoring agrees
the docs answered the question before the channel did
project: a forum for the local Linux group
editor: the editor i promised not to reconfigure this week
